Below is a highly advanced Keras project that is distinct from typical classification/regression tasks. It focuses on multimodal contrastive learning, combining image and tabular data in a self‑supervised framework—adapted from cutting‑edge research (e.g., CVPR 2023’s "Best of Both Worlds") (arxiv.org). The code is the core of the response, with minimal explanation outside it.

Project Title

ai-ml-ds-QtY3nCzKbfR – Multimodal Contrastive Learning with Keras

Filename: multimodal_contrastive_learning.py

📄 Short Description

Train separate encoders for image and tabular inputs using a contrastive (InfoNCE-style) loss to learn a shared representation space. Fine-tune on downstream tasks and optionally append labels as features (LaaF) for supervised contrastive improvements.

# multimodal_contrastive_learning.py

import tensorflow as tf
from tensorflow import keras
from tensorflow.keras import layers
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

# Load image + tabular dataset (STL-10 images + synthetic tabular features)
(x_img: np.ndarray, _), _ = keras.datasets.stl10.load_data()  # images
n: int = x_img.shape[0]
# Synthetic tabular of 10 continuous features
x_tab: np.ndarray = np.random.randn(n, 10).astype("float32")
img_size: tuple = (96, 96, 3)
x_img = tf.image.resize(x_img, img_size[:2]) / 255.0

# Define batch and contrastive settings
batch_size: int = 128
temperature: float = 0.1

# Tabular encoder
def build_tabular_encoder(input_dim: int =10) -> keras.Model:
    inp = keras.Input(shape=(input_dim,))
    x = layers.Dense(64, activation="relu")(inp)
    x = layers.Dense(32, activation="relu")(x)
    out = layers.Dense(16)(x)
    return keras.Model(inp, out, name="TabEncoder")

# Image encoder
def build_image_encoder(img_shape: tuple =img_size) -> keras.Model:
    inp = keras.Input(shape=img_shape)
    x = layers.Conv2D(32,3,activation="relu")(inp)
    x = layers.MaxPooling2D()(x)
    x = layers.Conv2D(64,3,activation="relu")(x)
    x = layers.GlobalAveragePooling2D()(x)
    out = layers.Dense(16)(x)
    return keras.Model(inp, out, name="ImgEncoder")

tab_enc: keras.Model = build_tabular_encoder()
img_enc: keras.Model = build_image_encoder()

# Projection heads to 16-d common space
proj_tab = keras.Sequential([layers.Dense(16), layers.Lambda(lambda x: tf.math.l2_normalize(x, axis=1))])
proj_img = keras.Sequential([layers.Dense(16), layers.Lambda(lambda x: tf.math.l2_normalize(x, axis=1))])

# Build contrastive model
inp_tab = keras.Input(shape=(10,), name="tab_input")
inp_img = keras.Input(shape=img_size, name="img_input")
h_tab = proj_tab(tab_enc(inp_tab))
h_img = proj_img(img_enc(inp_img))
model = keras.Model([inp_tab, inp_img], [h_tab, h_img])

# InfoNCE loss
class ContrastiveModel(keras.Model):
    def __init__(self, model, temp=0.1):
        super().__init__()
        self.model = model
        self.temp = temp

    def compile(self, optimizer):
        super().compile()
        self.opt = optimizer

    def contrastive_loss(self, z1, z2):
        logits = tf.matmul(z1, z2, transpose_b=True) / self.temp
        labels = tf.range(tf.shape(z1)[0])
        return (keras.losses.sparse_categorical_crossentropy(labels, logits, from_logits=True) +
                keras.losses.sparse_categorical_crossentropy(labels, tf.transpose(logits), from_logits=True)) / 2

    def train_step(self, data):
        x_tab_batch, x_img_batch = data
        with tf.GradientTape() as tape:
            z_tab, z_img = self.model([x_tab_batch, x_img_batch], training=True)
            loss = self.contrastive_loss(z_tab, z_img)
        grads = tape.gradient(loss, self.model.trainable_weights)
        self.opt.apply_gradients(zip(grads, self.model.trainable_weights))
        return {"loss": loss}

contrastive_model = ContrastiveModel(model, temperature)
contrastive_model.compile(optimizer=keras.optimizers.Adam(1e-3))

# Prepare dataset
dataset = tf.data.Dataset.from_tensor_slices((x_tab, x_img))
dataset = dataset.shuffle(1024).batch(batch_size)

# Pretrain
contrastive_model.fit(dataset, epochs=10)

# 🧰 Evaluate or fine‑tune on synthetic downstream task
y: np.ndarray = (x_tab[:,0] > 0).astype("int32")
tab_enc.trainable = False; img_enc.trainable = False
comb = layers.Concatenate()([tab_enc.output, img_enc.output])
out = layers.Dense(1, activation="sigmoid")(comb)
finetune = keras.Model([inp_tab, inp_img], out)
finetune.compile(loss="binary_crossentropy", optimizer="adam", metrics=["accuracy"])
x_tab_train, x_tab_val, x_img_train, x_img_val, y_train, y_val = train_test_split(
    x_tab, x_img, y, test_size=0.2
)
finetune.fit([x_tab_train, x_img_train], y_train, epochs=5,
             validation_data=([x_tab_val, x_img_val], y_val))

🧪 Example Inputs & Expected Outputs

  • Input (during retrieval):
    • Tabular row where feature0 > 0
    • Image from STL-10
  • Output:
    • During infonce pretraining: identical instance embeddings for image-tab pair
    • After fine-tuning: binary prediction (~0 or ~1) based on synthetic label
